correctness.rationale: For each intra-part nonedge in K_{n1,...,nr}, distance is exactly 2 and the common neighbors are the vertices outside that part. Thus S total-visible iff its complement C is not contained in any part U_i of size≥2. Inclusion–exclusion of a forbidden upward families yields F=(1+z)^N−Σ_{large i}z^{N−n_i}(1+z)^{n_i}+(a−1)z^N; minimal permitted complements are a singleton-part vertex or a pair crossing two large parts, giving M=bz^{N−1}+Σ_{i<j large}n_i n_j z^{N−2}. No-singleton case is dual rank-two partition-matroid independence complex; matroid shellability and reduced Euler characteristic give ∨^{a−1}S^{N−3} over integers. For b≥1 the explicit union (Δ_U*∂Δ_B)∪(K0*Δ_B) of two cones has intersection K0*∂Δ_B, giving b-fold suspension; a≤1 cases are contractible. Facet equicardinality proves exact purity/matroid boundary. Independently computed shortest paths with selected forbidden vertices for all subsets of seven distinct 3+-part profiles (including a=0,1 and nonpure a≥2,b≥1) and verified formula f-vectors and facet counts; finite BFS cannot prove homotopy or integral torsion-freeness.
residual_risks: Restricted to labelled finite complete multipartite graphs r≥3; empty-face convention, no canonical equivariant homotopy splitting. Mod-2 homology tests alone do not establish integer homotopy, which follows by shellability/gluing.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of total mutual-visibility simplicial complexes for the entire complete multipartite graph family is useful beyond its maximum cardinality: both labelled all-face and facet polynomials, exact matroidality/purity threshold and integral wedge homotopy are determined. Singleton classes furnish an instructive infinite nonpure sphere-wedge boundary while retaining a single homology dimension; this is mathematically motivated, not an arbitrary small slice.
residual_risks: Standard cut-complex machinery is essential and properly credited; the novelty is the combined specific classification rather than new general shellability theory.

limitations: Finite connected complete multipartite r≥3, not general graphs.
Historical priority risk from alternative cut-complex formulation retained.
